$comment: Curated reference set of EXISTING icons from the runtime snapshot, chosen to span structural categories. Rationales describe why each icon represents its category. Optical-correction entries are REVIEW candidates only: they flag icons that likely rely on optical adjustment, NOT verified corrections. No geometry is asserted as correct; all optical claims require rendered visual review. These are existing assets; nothing is generated.

references.rationale: Single horizontal stroke M6 12H18. The minimal case: one open path, no keyshape, no fill, round caps. Baseline for 'simplest valid icon'.

Single near-horizontal stroke with a non-integer endpoint (M21 11.9334H3). Representative of simple icons that nonetheless carry non-integer coordinates, which matters for duplicate/visual comparison.
Open polyline with two diagonal segments and a sharp interior vertex (M4 13L10 19L20 5). Canonical angular/diagonal open stroke.
Enclosed circle lens plus a diagonal handle stroke (M15 15L21 21). Two-path composition of an enclosed shape plus an open overlay stroke.
Pure enclosed circle keyshape, the clockwise 'M12 22C...' encoding. Reference for the circle keyshape variant A.
Circle keyshape using the counter-clockwise 'M2 12C...' encoding plus an inner checkmark. Reference for circle keyshape variant B AND for keyshape-first path ordering.
Pure enclosed sharp-cornered box (M3 21H21V3H3V21Z). Reference for the square keyshape at full canvas extent.
Ten-vertex closed star polygon with many diagonals. Standalone (no keyshape) complex angular shape.
references.optical_note: Stars commonly need optical vertical centering because the visual mass sits low; whether this asset applies such a shift is UNVERIFIED and needs rendered review.

references.rationale: Circle keyshape (variant A) plus an inset star using fill-rule evenodd. Reference for overlay-inside-keyshape composition and for inner-symbol safe-area inset.
Single closed organic curve with two rounded lobes and a bottom point. Reference for smooth Bezier-heavy rounded shapes.
references.optical_note: Hearts typically need optical centering; the point vs lobe balance should be reviewed visually. UNVERIFIED.

references.rationale: Shield outline plus an overlaid checkmark. KEY reference for the contradictory path ordering: the checkmark path is drawn BEFORE the shield outline, contradicting keyshape-first.
Padlock body/shackle plus a small overlaid checkmark, both using fill-rule evenodd compound paths. Reference for object+symbol overlay naming (object-symbol).
Rect-landscape envelope body plus a V flap overlay. Reference for the rect-landscape keyshape and a two-path container+detail split.
Leftward arrow (M12 6L6 12L12 18M6 12H18) using the double-dash directional suffix. Reference for directional naming AND for RTL mirroring questions.
Downward chevron (M18 9L12 15L6 9). Reference for a minimal directional open stroke and the directional '--' suffix overload.
Directional arrow enclosed in a circle keyshape, combining directional suffix with the -circled modifier semantics.
Trash can with a crossing diagonal stroke (M3 3L21 21) baked into a single multi-subpath 'd'. Reference for the -crossed/negation modifier and multi-subpath composition.
Speech-bubble outline plus an inner handset glyph, both fill-rule evenodd. Reference for brand-derived complex two-path icons.
Many-rayed sun burst plus an inner circle. Reference for radially symmetric complex geometry and optical centering of a central motif.
references.optical_note: Radial bursts rely on precise optical centering; UNVERIFIED whether the inner circle is optically vs geometrically centered.

references.rationale: One of only two icons wrapped in <g clip-path> with a <defs><clipPath><rect/></clipPath>. KEY reference for the clip-path/defs structural variant and the rect fill='white' mask-bound artifact.

Diamond sign with inner directional arrows, also wrapped in <g clip-path> with sub-pixel coordinates extending to the canvas edge (0.814..23.178). Second clip-path reference and a bounds-edge coordinate example.

Circle keyshape plus a plus symbol, stroked in #9747FF, the exact color the implementation guide documents for every path. It is the ONLY asset in the set that uses the guide's documented color; the other 600 use #333333 and are inconsistent with the guide. KEY reference for the stroke.color rule (documented #9747FF passes) and for the asset-stroke vs CSS-mask-currentColor scope distinction. The guide does not describe #9747FF as a placeholder or authoring color, and this entry does not either.

A plus drawn as a closed outlined cross (M18 10H14V6...Z) rather than two crossing strokes, achieving 'heavy' weight by geometry since stroke-width is never set. KEY reference that -heavy weight comes from outline geometry, not a stroke attribute, and must NOT be auto-exempted.
A box with a full diagonal X (M2.997 21.011L20.997 3.011...). Reference for an 'empty/none' semantic sentinel and a multi-subpath single path.
